news_drafts.headline: Denbighshire's 2027/28 budget gap would be £8m after a 5.3% council tax rise, down from May forecast
news_drafts.lead:
Denbighshire County Council's budget gap for 2027/28 would be £8m after a mid-range council tax rise of 5.3%, according to its medium term financial strategy and plan. The rise would yield an additional £4.7m, which the paper says addresses roughly a third of the funding gap. The paper, before the Performance Scrutiny Committee on 12 November, calls the remaining £8m "substantial" and says it has come down from the last forecast in May.

Over the three years from 2027/28 to 2029/30, the forecast gap ranges from a low of £19m to a high of £36m, with a mid-range projection of £27m. The paper says the figures are uncertain and that further work is needed to refine them. The plan's council tax assumptions for 2027/28 range from 4% to 7%.

The paper also sets out the council tax rises that would bridge the total gap under its low, medium and high scenarios: 11%, 15% and 20%. It describes these as theoretical and as assuming no savings are achieved. It says a 15% rise would in theory balance the budget without reductions, and that no decisions have been made.

news_drafts.headline: Denbighshire forecasts £5.2m overspend for 2026/27, with schools £5.4m over budget
news_drafts.lead:
Denbighshire County Council's Cabinet was told on 20 October that the council expects to end 2026/27 having spent £314.1m against a budget of £308.9m, a forecast overspend of £5.2m, or 1.7%. A forecast overspend is where a council expects to finish the year having spent more than it budgeted.

The schools budget, including the part of school funding the council does not pass directly to schools, is forecast at £103.9m against a budget of £98.5m. That is £5.4m, or 5.4%, over. It is the largest variance of any service in the budget summary, and it is larger than the overspend for the council as a whole.

The council's savings programme, the cuts and efficiencies it has committed to in order to balance its budget, set a target of £3.17m for 2026/27. The savings tracker shows £1.82m achieved, or 57.4%. A further £701k, 22.1%, is in progress. Proposals worth £648k, 20.4%, are marked "not achieved", and £738k of the target remains undelivered. The papers set out the figures but, in the extracts available, do not say how the council plans to close the gap.

news_drafts.headline: Denbighshire revised corporate income forecast down by £28.2m to £1.1m and matched cuts to expenditure, keeping overall budget overspend at £510k
news_drafts.lead: Denbighshire Council has revised its corporate income forecast from £29.3m to £1.1m mid-year and made equivalent cuts to expenditure, leaving its net budget position unchanged. The £28.2m reduction in expected income — roughly nine-tenths of what was budgeted — has been matched by spending reductions of the same scale, keeping the council's overall budget overspend at £510k (0.2%) against a total budget of £309m. The adjustment reflects changed circumstances for income sources, though the council has not detailed which. Service-level overspends are modest: Adult Social Care and Homelessness, the largest service budget at £67.8m, is forecast to overspend by £442k; Planning, Public Protection and Countryside by £268k on a £12.2m budget. The overall position has deteriorated by £402k from the previous forecast.

findings.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary
findings.headline: Planning, Public Protection and Countryside is projected at £12,313k against a £12,457k budget, a £144k (1.2%) underspend, compared with a £188k overspend previously.
findings.detail: Projected expenditure is £20,989k against a £20,581k budget, and projected income is £8,676k against £8,124k. The line has moved from a £188k projected overspend to a £144k projected underspend.
findings.matters: A service that has moved from overspend to underspend between reports is a change a peer finance team would want to understand, and the paper records the movement without giving its cause.

findings.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary
findings.headline: Adult Social Care and Homelessness is projected at £68,305k against a £67,858k budget, a £447k (0.7%) variance, compared with £442k previously.
findings.detail: Projected expenditure is £83,554k against a £91,659k budget, and projected income is £15,249k against £23,801k. Income is projected £8,552k below budget, and expenditure is projected £8,105k below budget.
findings.matters: This is the only service line other than schools with a net projected overspend, and it coincides with income projected well below budget, which a finance director at another social care authority would compare with their own charging income.
findings.figures: Budget £67,858k; projected £68,305k; variance £447k (0.7%); previous £442k; expenditure variance -£8,105k; income variance £8,552k.

findings.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary
findings.headline: The Corporate budget is projected at £21,499k against a £22,218k budget, a £719k (3.2%) underspend, unchanged from the previous figure.
findings.detail: Projected expenditure is £22,631k against a £51,490k budget, and projected income is £1,132k against £29,272k. The variance of -£719k is the same as in the previous figure.
findings.matters: This corporate underspend is one of the offsets within the total, and its gross figures show expenditure and income both well below budget.
findings.figures: Budget £22,218k; projected £21,499k; variance -£719k (-3.2%); previous -£719k; expenditure variance -£28,859k; income variance £28,140k.

findings.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary
findings.headline: Council services and corporate budget is projected at £209,686k against a £210,380k budget, a £694k (0.3%) underspend, compared with £167k previously.
findings.detail: This line excludes schools and is projected under budget, with the previous figure showing a £167k underspend. Its movement is larger than in the previous figure.
findings.matters: This is the part of the council budget outside schools, and it is the figure that partly offsets the schools variance in the total.

findings.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary
findings.headline: The total council budget is projected at £313,563k against a £308,905k budget, a £4,659k (1.5%) variance, compared with £5,185k previously.
findings.detail: The total combines council services and corporate budgets, which are projected under budget, with the schools line, which is projected over budget. The variance in the previous figure was £5,185k.
findings.matters: This is the headline net position for the year, and the movement from £5,185k to £4,659k is the change a reader would track from one report to the next.

daily_post.headline: Fixed penalty notices for school attendance do not generate a high level of income for the Education Service.
daily_post.lead: A council may assume enforcement income offsets service costs; this paper records that it does not, which matters to finance officers assessing similar income streams.
